items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: So I did, I went back to join him in Boston, to Roseland Square Ballroom I think. Billie Holiday was in the band. And I stayed in that band until I joined the Glenn Miller band.

ctx.x: So you never at that point got into the New York Local. Because they just pulled your card and you had to start over?

Well in a way I’m glad I didn’t. You know, because the way it turned out it was good. And you get mad — I got mad at Artie. He had a recording date and this was in the 1937 band, September. And I’d been in that band too. But after the union card thing, I was not too friendly. So he had one of those transcription dates in New York. Like we’d play in Wildwood, New Jersey, a summer resort, and this was September I guess, at the end of the summer. And there was a new tune out, I can’t remember the name of it, and my…
You did some traveling in the south with Artie Shaw? When Billie Holiday was in the band, didn’t you?

items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then there was Johnny Best, also. And George Arus.

ctx.x: When you changed, when you got the new band, how did you go about picking the guys, selecting the musicians?

I listened to people. I went around and listened to people. I couldn’t afford to get the ones I wanted. I would have grabbed Harry James. I’d heard him with Benny Pollack. I knew Benny. But I couldn’t. I couldn’t afford him. Benny Goodman got him. So I had to train guys. I had to find guys who could play. I could hear them trying to do something. Les Robinson has called me and said, “You changed my whole life.” He said, “I don’t know what you heard in me.” I heard him trying. He had no sound, but he could . . .…
